title: Kinetic Particle Model of Matter
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Kinetic Particle Model of Matter Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_code: O-Level Physics (6091): Kinetic Particle Model of Matter
standard_text: Compare the properties of solids, liquids and gases; describe qualitatively the molecular structure of solids, liquids and gases in terms of the arrangement, separation and motion of the particles and the forces between them; infer from Brownian motion that particles are in constant random motion; relate the rise in temperature of a body to an increase in the average kinetic energy of its particles; explain the pressure of a gas in terms of particles colliding with the walls, and describe qualitatively the effect of changing temperature and volume on the pressure of a fixed mass of gas (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on the kinetic particle model of matter: solids, liquids and gases, temperature and kinetic energy, Brownian motion, diffusion and gas pressure. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: All matter is made of moving particles.
key_sub: Gas pressure comes from particles hitting the walls.
body_html:
How to think about it

All matter is made of tiny particles in constant random motion.

  • Solid: close, regular, vibrate about fixed positions, strong forces. Liquid: close, random, slide past each other. Gas: far apart, random, fast, negligible forces.
  • A higher temperature means a higher average kinetic energy of the particles.
  • Brownian motion: visible smoke particles jiggle because invisible air particles hit them unevenly.
  • Gas pressure: particles hit the walls. Hotter gas or smaller volume means more frequent (and harder) collisions, so higher pressure.
Example

A sealed tin of air is heated. Pressure?

particles move faster

more frequent, harder collisions with the walls

Answer: increases

Example

A syringe of air is pushed in at constant temperature. Pressure?

same particles, smaller volume

more collisions per second

Answer: increases

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the particles themselves expand when heated. They move faster and further apart.
  • Saying gas pressure is caused by particles hitting each other. It is caused by particles hitting the walls.
  • Saying particles in a solid do not move. They vibrate.
  • Thinking the smoke particles in Brownian motion move by themselves.

faq.q: What is the kinetic particle model of matter?
faq.a: The idea that all matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving randomly; their arrangement and motion explain the properties of solids, liquids and gases.
That air (or water) particles are moving randomly, because they knock the visible smoke particles about in a random, jerky way.

faq.q: Why does the pressure of a gas rise when it is heated in a closed container?
faq.a: The particles gain kinetic energy and move faster, so they hit the walls more often and with greater force.

items.q: Why is a gas easy to compress?

items.q: A drop of ink is added to a beaker of still water. After an hour the water is evenly coloured. What is the best explanation?
c: Diffusion: ink particles moved from a higher to a lower concentration.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.

The particles were pushed by convection only.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.
